requirements.title: Enqueue a durable job with dedup
requirements.rationale: A caller asks for work once and must be able to trust that it is recorded, and that a workspace never accumulates pending jobs.

criteria.condition: Enqueue is called inside a store transaction for a job type and a workspace that has no job of that type in queued, running or failed
criteria.action: store a new job with status queued, retry_count 0, the given payload document, a null result document and created_at and updated_at equal to the clock's present, as part of that transaction, and return it
criteria.contract: returns the job {id: a version 4 UUID, type, workspace_slug, status: 'queued', retry_count: 0, next_attempt_at: null, error: null, completed_at: null} and a nil error; the job is visible to other readers only after the caller's transaction commits

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go: tx = store.begin(); j, err = q.Enqueue(tx, 'probe', 'w', payload); assert err == nil; assert j.status == 'queued' and j.retry_count == 0 and j.next_attempt_at == null and j.completed_at == null; assert j.id matches the UUID v4 pattern; assert q.Get(j.id) from outside the transaction is not found; tx.commit(); assert q.Get(j.id).payload == payload; a second case rolls the transaction back and asserts the job does not exist

criteria.condition: Enqueue is called for a job type and a workspace that already has a job of that type in queued, running or failed
criteria.action: store nothing and report a duplicate that names the existing job
criteria.contract: returns a duplicate error from which the caller reads the existing job's id (errors.As to the queue's duplicate error type); the number of jobs of the workspace is unchanged

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go, a table over the existing job's status {queued, running, failed}: _, err = q.Enqueue(tx, 'probe', 'w', p); assert err is the duplicate error and its job id == existing.id; assert count(jobs of 'w') == 1. Further rows where the enqueue succeeds: existing job completed, dead_letter or cancelled; existing pending job of workspace 'other'; existing pending job of 'w' with another job type

criteria.condition: several Enqueue calls for the same job type and workspace run at the same time in separate transactions
criteria.action: let exactly one of them store a job and report a duplicate to every other
criteria.contract: exactly one call returns a job; each other call returns the duplicate error or, when its transaction lost a write conflict, is retried by the queue until it returns the duplicate error; one job of the workspace exists afterwards

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store file in t.TempDir()
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go: start 16 goroutines that each begin a transaction, call q.Enqueue(tx, 'probe', 'w', p) and commit on success; assert exactly 1 success and 15 duplicate errors naming the winner's id; assert count(jobs of 'w') == 1

criteria.condition: a follow-up enqueue names a job of the same type and workspace that is running, and that job is the only job of the workspace in queued, running or failed
criteria.action: store the follow-up as a new queued job
criteria.contract: returns the new job with status 'queued' and an id different from the named job's

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go: a = enqueue and claim a job of 'w' whose handler blocks; f, err = q.EnqueueFollowUp(tx, a.id, payload); assert err == nil; assert f.status == 'queued' and f.id != a.id and f.type == a.type and f.workspace_slug == 'w'

criteria.condition: a follow-up enqueue names a job that is not running, or names a running job while another job of the workspace is already queued or failed
criteria.action: store nothing and report a duplicate
criteria.contract: returns the duplicate error naming a pending job of the workspace when one exists; returns a not-found error when the named job does not exist; the number of jobs is unchanged

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/enqueue_test.go, a table: {named job queued, named job failed, named job completed with another job queued, named job running and a follow-up already queued} -> duplicate error; {unknown job id} -> not-found error; in every row count(jobs) is unchanged

criteria.action: for any job whose enqueueing transaction committed, return the same job, with the same id, payload and status, after the store is closed and opened again

setup: a real store file in t.TempDir()
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/store_test.go: enqueue three jobs for three workspaces and commit; close the store; open it again at the same path; build a new queue; for each: assert q.Get(id) equals the job returned at enqueue in id, type, workspace_slug, status, payload, created_at

requirements.title: Run queued jobs on workers
requirements.rationale: The hub executes its own jobs, a few at a time, and never two for one workspace.

criteria.condition: a dispatcher pass finds a queued job whose type has a registered handler, while fewer than 4 jobs are running and no job of the same type and workspace is running
criteria.action: claim the job by setting its status to running and emptying its result document, and call the handler once with the job and a context
criteria.contract: the handler receives the job with status 'running' and its payload; a concurrent read of the job shows status 'running', result null and updated_at at the clock's present

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it; the handler blocks until released
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: j = enqueue('probe','w', p); q.Pass(); wait until the handler is entered; assert handler.calls == [j.id] and the job it received has status 'running' and payload p; assert q.Get(j.id).status == 'running' and result == null

criteria.condition: a job is queued while the queue runs with its background dispatcher and a worker is free
criteria.action: start the job's handler within 5 seconds
criteria.contract: the handler is called no later than 5 seconds after the enqueueing transaction committed

setup: a queue over a real store file in t.TempDir() with a handler for 'probe'
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: start q.Run(ctx) with the real clock and the default dispatcher interval; t0 = now; enqueue and commit; wait for the handler call with a 5 s deadline; assert it arrived; a second case enqueues without waking the dispatcher (the wake is disabled by a test option) and asserts the call still arrives within 5 s

criteria.condition: 4 jobs are running
criteria.action: claim no further job, and claim the next queued job on the first dispatcher pass after one of the 4 has ended
criteria.contract: at no moment are more than 4 handlers running; the fifth job stays 'queued' until a running job is settled

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it; each handler blocks until released
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: enqueue jobs for workspaces w1..w6; q.Pass(); assert 4 handlers entered and jobs 5 and 6 are 'queued'; q.Pass() again; assert still 4; release handler 1; q.Pass(); assert job 5 is 'running' and job 6 'queued'; assert the maximum number of handlers observed running together == 4

criteria.condition: a job of a type and workspace is running
criteria.action: leave every queued job of the same type and workspace unclaimed, and claim it on the first dispatcher pass after the running job has ended
criteria.contract: the follow-up's handler call begins after the running job's settlement committed

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: a = enqueue('probe','w') and claim it (handler blocks); f = q.EnqueueFollowUp(tx, a.id, p); q.Pass(); assert f is 'queued' and handler.calls == [a.id]; release a; q.Pass(); assert q.Get(a.id).status == 'completed' and f is 'running'

criteria.action: for any queued job, let at most one worker claim it, however many dispatcher passes run at the same time
criteria.contract: the handler is called exactly once per transition from queued to running

setup: a queue over a real store file in t.TempDir()
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: enqueue one job; run 16 goroutines that each call q.Pass() at the same moment; release the handler; assert handler.calls has length 1; repeat for 50 jobs on 50 workspaces with the limit of 4 and assert every job id appears exactly once in handler.calls when all are completed

criteria.action: claim queued jobs in the order of created_at ascending, then id ascending

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: with the limit of 4 filled by blocking jobs, enqueue x at t, y at t+1s, z at t+1s for three further workspaces; release one running job at a time with a pass after each; assert the claim order is x, then the smaller id of {y, z}, then the other

criteria.condition: no handler is registered for a queued job's type
criteria.action: leave the job queued and unchanged on every dispatcher pass, and claim it on the first pass after a handler for its type is registered
criteria.contract: the job's status stays 'queued' and its updated_at does not change; the pass reports no error

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: j = enqueue('nohandler','w'); q.Pass(); q.Pass(); assert q.Get(j.id) equals j; q.Register('nohandler', h); q.Pass(); assert h.calls == [j.id]

criteria.condition: a dispatcher pass finds a failed job whose next_attempt_at is at or before the clock's present
criteria.action: set the job's status to queued and its next_attempt_at to null, keeping retry_count and error, and treat it in the same pass like any queued job
criteria.contract: one second before next_attempt_at the job is still 'failed' and its handler is not called; at next_attempt_at the handler is called a second time with the same job id

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: run one attempt that fails retryably at T (next_attempt_at == T+4s); clock = T+3s; q.Pass(); assert status 'failed' and handler.calls has length 1; clock = T+4s; q.Pass(); assert handler.calls has length 2 and the job it received has retry_count 1 and error set; a variant with all 4 workers busy asserts the job is 'queued' with next_attempt_at null after the pass

requirements.title: Settle the outcome of an attempt
requirements.rationale: A failure that may pass is retried with growing delays; one that cannot pass ends the job at once, where a person can look at it and requeue it.

criteria.condition: the handler of a running job returns nil
criteria.action: set the job's status to completed, clear error and the failure detail, set completed_at to the clock's present, leave next_attempt_at null and keep the result document the handler stored
criteria.contract: a read of the job returns status 'completed', error null, detail null, completed_at set, retry_count unchanged

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: a job that failed once retryably (retry_count 1, error set) runs again and its handler stores result R and returns nil; assert status == 'completed'; error == null; detail == null; completed_at == clock.now; retry_count == 1; result == R

criteria.condition: the handler of a running job returns an error that is not marked permanent, and the job's retry_count is below 20
criteria.action: set the job's status to failed, raise retry_count by one to n, set next_attempt_at to the clock's present plus min(2 seconds × 2 to the power n, 2 hours), store the error's text in error, replace the failure detail by the one the error carries or clear it, and leave completed_at null
criteria.contract: after the n-th retryable failure next_attempt_at − now is 4 s for n=1, 8 s for n=2, 16 s for n=3, 4096 s for n=11, 7200 s for n=12 and 7200 s for n=20

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go, a table over retry_count before the attempt {0, 1, 2, 10, 11, 19}: settle a retryable error 'boom'; assert status == 'failed'; retry_count == before+1; next_attempt_at − clock.now == {4s, 8s, 16s, 4096s, 7200s, 7200s}; error == 'boom'; completed_at == null. One more row: an error carrying detail D after a failure that stored detail C -> detail == D; then an error with no detail -> detail == null

criteria.condition: the handler of a running job returns an error that is not marked permanent, and the job's retry_count is 20
criteria.action: set the job's status to dead_letter with retry_count still 20, store the error's text, set completed_at and leave next_attempt_at null
criteria.contract: a read returns status 'dead_letter', retry_count 20, next_attempt_at null, completed_at set; no later dispatcher pass calls the handler for this job

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: drive one job through 20 retryable failures, advancing the clock to each next_attempt_at; assert it is 'failed' with retry_count 20; advance and fail a 21st time; assert status == 'dead_letter' and retry_count == 20 and completed_at != null and next_attempt_at == null; advance the clock by 3 h and run a pass; assert handler.calls has length 21

criteria.condition: the handler of a running job returns an error marked permanent
criteria.action: set the job's status to dead_letter without changing retry_count, store the error's text and the detail document the error carries, set completed_at and never retry the job
criteria.contract: a read returns status 'dead_letter', retry_count as before the attempt, error the text, detail the document, completed_at set, next_attempt_at null

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go, a table over retry_count before {0, 3}: the handler returns jobs.Permanent(err 'conflict') carrying detail D; assert status == 'dead_letter'; retry_count == before; error == 'conflict'; detail == D; completed_at == clock.now; advance 3 h; q.Pass(); assert the handler was not called again

criteria.condition: the handler of a running job panics
criteria.action: recover the panic, settle the attempt as a retryable failure whose error text contains the panic value, and keep serving other jobs
criteria.contract: the job is 'failed' (or 'dead_letter' when retry_count was 20) with error containing the panic value; the process does not exit; a job of another workspace queued afterwards completes

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: the handler panics with 'kaboom' for workspace 'w'; q.Pass(); assert q.Get(j.id).status == 'failed' and error contains 'kaboom' and retry_count == 1; enqueue a job for 'w2' with a handler result of nil; q.Pass(); assert it is 'completed'

criteria.condition: an attempt is settled and the job's type registered a settlement hook
criteria.action: call the hook once inside the store transaction of the settlement, with the job as the settlement leaves it and a flag that is true only when the new status is failed
criteria.contract: what the hook writes through the transaction is committed together with the job's new status; the flag is true for 'failed' and false for 'completed' and 'dead_letter'

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it; the handler's type also registers a recording settlement hook
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go, a table over outcomes {nil, retryable error, permanent error, retryable error at retry_count 20}: the hook writes a marker row through the transaction it is given and records its arguments; assert hook calls == 1; hook.job.status == {'completed','failed','dead_letter','dead_letter'}; hook.will_retry == {false,true,false,false}; assert the marker row exists exactly when the job has the new status

criteria.condition: the settlement hook returns an error or panics
criteria.action: undo the hook's own writes, log the failure with the job id, and commit the settlement without them
criteria.contract: the job has its new status; no row the hook wrote exists; the next dispatcher pass proceeds

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go, a table {hook returns an error after writing a marker row, hook panics after writing a marker row}: settle a success; assert q.Get(j.id).status == 'completed'; assert the marker row does not exist; assert the log holds one entry naming j.id; a queued job of another workspace is claimed on the next pass

criteria.condition: the handler stores a result document on its job while the job is running
criteria.action: replace the job's result document and make it visible to readers at once
criteria.contract: a read of the job during the run returns the last stored document; storing on a job that is not running returns a not-running error and changes nothing

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/settle_test.go: inside the handler: q.SetResult(ctx, j.id, R1); the test reads q.Get(j.id).result == R1 while the handler blocks; q.SetResult(ctx, j.id, R2); read == R2; release; after completion result == R2; then q.SetResult(ctx, j.id, R3) returns the not-running error and result is still R2; a later claim of a requeued job shows result null

requirements.title: Recover after a crash and stop at shutdown
requirements.rationale: A job must not be lost or stuck because the hub stopped while it ran.

criteria.condition: the queue's start hook runs and the store holds jobs with status running
criteria.action: set each of them to queued with retry_count, error, payload and created_at unchanged, before the dispatcher makes its first pass, and leave jobs in every other status untouched
criteria.contract: the hook returns nil; afterwards no job is 'running'; a job that was 'failed' keeps its next_attempt_at

setup: a real store file in t.TempDir()
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it; handlers of the first queue block for ever
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: with a first queue, bring jobs into {running with retry_count 0, running with retry_count 3 and an error text, failed, queued, completed, dead_letter, cancelled}; abandon that queue without settling; close and reopen the store; q2 = new queue; assert q2.Recover(ctx) == nil; assert both running jobs are 'queued' with retry_count {0, 3} and the error text kept; assert the five others are unchanged field by field

criteria.condition: the dispatcher runs after a recovery that returned a job to queued
criteria.action: claim the job and call its handler again from the start with the same job id and payload and an empty result document
criteria.contract: the handler is called once by the new queue for that job; when it returns nil the job is 'completed' with the retry_count it had before the stop

setup: a real store file in t.TempDir()
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: queue 1 claims job j (payload P), its handler stores result R and then blocks for ever; abandon queue 1, close and reopen the store; q2 = new queue with a handler that returns nil; q2.Recover(ctx); q2.Pass(); assert handler2.calls == [j.id] and the job it received has payload P and result null and retry_count 0; assert q2.Get(j.id).status == 'completed' and retry_count == 0

criteria.condition: the hub's shutdown reaches the queue while handlers are running
criteria.action: claim no further job, wait up to 30 seconds for the running handlers, settle the outcome of each handler that returns in that time, and stop when all have returned
criteria.contract: the queue's run function returns as soon as the last running handler has returned and was settled; a job queued before or during the shutdown stays 'queued'

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: start q.Run(ctx) with a controlled clock; job a is running (handler blocks), job b is queued for another workspace behind a full limit or enqueued after the cancel; cancel ctx; assert Run has not returned; q.Pass() has no effect: b stays 'queued'; release a's handler with nil; assert Run returns; assert a is 'completed' and b is 'queued' and b's handler was never called

criteria.condition: a handler is still running 30 seconds after the shutdown reached the queue
criteria.action: cancel that handler's context, stop without settling the attempt, and leave the job with status running in the store
criteria.contract: the run function returns at 30 seconds; the job's status, retry_count and error are as they were while it ran; an outcome the handler returns afterwards is dropped

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/lifecycle_test.go: job a is running with a handler that waits for its context; cancel the run context; advance the clock 29 s; assert Run has not returned and the handler's context is not done; advance to 30 s; assert the handler's context is done and Run returns; let the handler return an error; assert q.Get(a.id).status == 'running' and retry_count == 0 and error == null

requirements.title: Count jobs and remove them with their workspace
requirements.rationale: Operators watch the depth of the queue, and a deleted workspace must leave no job behind.

criteria.condition: a caller asks the queue for its depth
criteria.action: return, for every registered job type, the number of jobs in each of the statuses queued, running, failed, completed, dead_letter and cancelled, with 0 for a status that has none
criteria.contract: a map from job type to the six statuses, each with a count; all six keys are present for every registered type, also when the type has no job

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/queue_test.go: register 'probe' and 'rebuild'; bring 'probe' jobs into queued x2, running x1, failed x1, completed x3, dead_letter x1, cancelled x1; d = q.Depth(ctx); assert d['probe'] == {queued:2, running:1, failed:1, completed:3, dead_letter:1, cancelled:1}; assert d['rebuild'] has the six keys, all 0

criteria.condition: the workspace removal calls the queue's remover for a workspace slug inside its store transaction
criteria.action: delete every job of that workspace, of every type and status, as part of that transaction, and leave the jobs of other workspaces
criteria.contract: after the commit no job of the workspace is readable and an enqueue for the same slug succeeds; after a rollback every job is as before

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/store_test.go: jobs of 'w' in {queued, failed, completed, dead_letter} and one job of 'other'; tx = begin; q.RemoveWorkspace(tx, 'w'); tx.rollback(); assert 4 jobs of 'w' exist; tx = begin; q.RemoveWorkspace(tx, 'w'); tx.commit(); assert q.List('w') is empty and q.Get(id) is not found for each; assert the job of 'other' is unchanged; assert q.Enqueue(tx2, 'probe', 'w', p) succeeds

criteria.condition: a handler is running for a job whose workspace's jobs were removed
criteria.action: cancel the handler's context when the removal has committed and drop the handler's outcome without creating a job record
criteria.contract: the handler's context is done after the removal; when the handler returns, no job of the workspace exists, the settlement hook is not called and the dispatcher's next pass reports no error

setup: a queue of internal/jobs over a real store opened in t.TempDir(), a controlled clock, and no background dispatcher: the test runs single dispatcher passes
a scripted handler registered for the job type 'probe' that records every call and returns what the case tells it
check.pseudocode: in internal/jobs/store_test.go: job a of 'w' is running with a handler that waits for its context; remove 'w' and commit; assert the handler's context is done; the handler returns an error; assert q.Get(a.id) is not found; assert hook calls == 0; q.Pass() returns no error

requirements.title: Submit a rebuild
requirements.rationale: A developer or an agent asks for a rebuild once and gets a job to follow.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access (and, for a PAT, the scope rebuilds:write) sends POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild for a ready carry-patch workspace that has at least one patch in active or conflict and no rebuild job in queued, running or failed
criteria.action: queue a rebuild job whose strategy and fail mode are the body's values, or the workspace settings rebuild_strategy and rebuild_fail_mode for a value that is omitted, null or an empty string, whose integration_branch is the workspace's and whose submitted_by is the caller's user id, and answer with the rebuild job record
criteria.contract: HTTP 202 with the rebuild job record: status 'queued', retry_count 0, next_attempt_at, error, conflict, completed_at, upstream_head_sha, integration_head_sha and previous_integration_head_sha null, the four patches_ counts 0, integration_branch_pushed false, patch_results [], created_at and updated_at RFC 3339 UTC with whole seconds; every field of the record is present

setup: a hub router over a real store with the rebuild routes mounted, a ready carry-patch workspace 'w' owned by user U with integration branch 'deploy', and patches as the case states; no handler is registered for the job type 'rebuild', so queued jobs stay queued unless the test moves them through the queue
one patch with status active; a second table row uses a workspace whose only non-deleted patch has status conflict

criteria.contract: stdout holds exactly one JSON document, the record with status 'completed'; exit status 0; a record with status 'failed' never ends the wait

criteria.condition: a wait started by parley rebuild submit --wait or parley rebuild requeue --wait ends in dead_letter or cancelled, or passes its --timeout
criteria.action: print the final job record when there is one, report the failure of the wait and exit 1
criteria.contract: dead_letter or cancelled: stdout is the final record, stderr the envelope with error_type 'wait_failed', exit status 1; timeout: stdout empty, stderr the envelope with error_type 'wait_timeout', exit status 1, and no cancel request is sent

execution_paths.title: A developer submits a rebuild and waits through a retry

steps.action: runs parley rebuild submit <slug> --wait on a carry-patch workspace with one active patch
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/rebuild
stores the job as queued together with parley.rebuild.enqueue and answers 202 with the job record
claims the job on a worker and runs the handler, which fails with a retryable error; the job becomes failed with retry_count 1 and next_attempt_at 4 seconds later
polls GET /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/rebuilds/<id>, sees failed and keeps polling
returns the job to queued when next_attempt_at is reached, runs the handler again and settles the job as completed
prints the final job record with status completed and exits 0

execution_paths.title: An agent cancels a queued rebuild and requeues a dead-lettered one

steps.action: sends POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild; the handler fails with a permanent error
settles the job as dead_letter with the error text and the failure detail
sends POST /workspaces/:slug/rebuild again and receives 202 with a second job, then POST requeue of the first job
answers the requeue with 409 concurrent_rebuild because the second job is queued
sends DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rebuilds/<second id> twice
answers 200 with status cancelled and parley.rebuild.cancel, then 409 job_not_cancellable
sends POST requeue of the first job again
answers 200 with status queued, retry_count 0, error and conflict null, and writes parley.rebuild.requeue
